newsitem.title: IRAN: Iraqi Kurdish refugees in Iran near disaster - MSF.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish refugees in Iran near disaster - MSF.

text.p: Children of Iraqi Kurdish refugees in Iranian mountain camps are dying of cold and urgent international aid is needed to save the 65,000 refugees from a catastrophe, a medical charity said on Wednesday.

"The 65,000 Kurdish refugees here are a step away from human disaster. Every night one child dies in Kileh camp due to the cold," said Sotiris Papaspyropoulos, Medecins Sans Frontieres (MSF, Doctors Without Borders) chief of mission.

"We have two messages: immediate relocation and urgent mobility in the international community...to prevent the coming disaster," he told reporters in Tehran. "We have seen very little mobility in international donors in this crisis."
Tens of thousands of Iraqi Kurds have been sheltering in Iran or in a border buffer zone since fleeing fighting which erupted between Kurdish factions in northern Iraq in late August.

Papaspyropoulos said MSF, with an expatriate staff of 25, was the only international non-governmental organisation which has had a daily presence in seven of the eight refugee camps since the beginning of the crisis.
He said he knew of six cases of refugees who were wounded by land-mine explosions in border areas.
Iran said in early November it had spent 70 billion rials ($23.3 million) on the refugees, of which 15 billion rials were provided by the United Nations.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
